sanskrit: tattūṣṇīṃ bhava mā kaścidetacchroṣyasi te vacaḥ / tato mṛgāṅkadattātvaṃ śūrādaśivamāpsyasi // evam uktavatīṃ tāṃ ca jāraḥ kṣattā na cakṣame / pāpe mṛgāṅkadatte tvaṃ baddhabhāvādhunā dhruvam // tadasyānubhavedānīmadhikṣepasya me phalam / ity uktvā ca sa hantuṃ tāmuttasthau sāsidhenukaḥ //
english: So be silent, lest someone hears this speech of yours, and then you would certainly meet with calamity at the hands of Mṛgāṅkadatta, who is a brave man.” When she said this, her paramour, the warder, lost his temper with her. He said: “Wretched woman! you are certainly in love with Mṛgāṅkadatta, so receive now from me the just recompense of that taunt.” And he rose up to kill her, dagger in hand.
